ev.q: In 2001, an estimated 17,537 (95% CI=12,319--22,755) children aged < 14 years were treated in EDs for choking-related episodes
for a rate of 29.9 per 100,000 population (95% CI=21.0--38.8)
10,438 (59.5%; 95% CI=39.3%--79.7%) were treated for choking on a food substance
1,844 (10.5%; 95% CI=3.1--18.0) were hospitalized or transferred to a facility with a higher level of care.
Rates were highest for infants aged <1 year (140.4) and decreased with age.
CDC analyzed data from the National Electronic Injury Surveillance System-All Injury Program

methods_quotes.q: Each case was assigned a sample weight based on the inverse probability of selection
Confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated by using a direct variance estimation procedure that accounted for the sample weights and complex sample design.
Rates were calculated by using 2001 U.S. Census Bureau population estimates.
Estimates might be unstable because the coefficient of variation is >30%.
